record.paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: Let M_ε be a channel whose output is always ε-close to the maximally mixed state, in the sense ||M_ε(ρ) − I/d|| < ε, and define its polarization Φ_{x,ε} = x I + (1−x) M_ε. For maximal output p-norm multiplicativity, ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), does Φ_{x,ε} satisfy this property for 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, at least when ε is sufficiently small? If it does not always satisfy the property, for which values of x and p does it hold, and how do those values depend on ε?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix a finite dimension d ≥ 2 and let M_d denote the algebra of d×d complex matrices. A quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map Φ : M_d → M_d. For a state ρ (density operator) and 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, the Schatten p-norm of Φ(ρ) is ‖Φ(ρ)‖_p = (Tr|Φ(ρ)|^p)^{1/p}, and the maximal output p-norm of Φ is

  ν_p(Φ) = sup_ρ ‖Φ(ρ)‖_p,

where the supremum is over density operators on C^d. The channel Φ is said to satisfy maximal output p-norm multiplicativity if, for every quantum channel Ω (acting on any finite-dimensional matrix algebra),

  ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ) · ν_p(Ω).   (*)

For ε > 0, let M_ε be a quantum channel on M_d whose output is always ε-close to the maximally mixed state in the sense that for every density operator ρ,

  ‖M_ε(ρ) − I/d‖ < ε

(in the operator norm). For x ∈ [0,1] define the "polarized" channel

  Φ_{x,ε}(ρ) = x ρ + (1 − x) M_ε(ρ).

Question. Does Φ_{x,ε} satisfy the multiplicativity identity (*) for all 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, at least when ε is sufficiently small? If not, determine for which values of x ∈ [0,1] and p ∈ [1,2] the identity (*) holds for Φ_{x,ε}, and describe the dependence of these values on ε.
artifact.status_search_result: The general maximal output p-norm multiplicativity conjecture has been refuted: Hayden–Winter and Hastings showed that for every p > 1 there exist quantum channels (built from random unitaries that produce nearly-maximally-mixed outputs, very much in the spirit of the M_ε construction) whose maximal output p-norm is not multiplicative. Thus the strong form of the question for p > 1 fails in general. The case p = 1 is trivial (ν_1 ≡ 1). The fine question of exactly which (x, p, ε)-regimes for the polarized channels Φ_{x,ε} preserve multiplicativity does not appear to have a complete published answer; partial results for qubit and depolarizing-type channels exist but a full characterization remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Counterexamples to the maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture for all p > 1
status_evidence.snippet: For all p > 1, there exist channels (random-unitary constructions producing outputs close to the maximally mixed state) whose maximal output p-norm is not multiplicative.
status_evidence.claim: The general multiplicativity conjecture is false for every p > 1, including the range 1 < p ≤ 2.

status_evidence.title: The maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture is false
status_evidence.snippet: Hastings disproves multiplicativity using random channels close to noise.
status_evidence.claim: Multiplicativity fails in general; the specific polarized-channel case remains a refined open question.

status_evidence.title: Notes on multiplicativity of maximal output purity for completely positive qubit maps
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multiplicativity for qubit maps with partial results.
status_evidence.claim: Partial multiplicativity results exist for restricted channel classes.
